Medea. The sorceress princess who used her magic to help a hero she loved, only to become a tragic and fearsome figure when he abandoned her.

Medea was the princess of Colchis and daughter of Aeetes. The gods themselves trained her in the magical arts and venoms. When Jason arrived seeking the Golden Fleece, she fell madly in love with him. Abandoning her loyalty to her father for passion, she used her magical knowledge to help Jason complete the seemingly impossible tasks set by her father, including taming fire-breathing bulls.

Medea fled Colchis with Jason and the Argonauts, carrying with her the Golden Fleece and the weight of her betrayal. To delay her father's pursuit, she even murdered her own brother Apsyrtus. She married Jason and bore him children, building a life with the man she had sacrificed everything to help. But years later, Jason abandoned her for a political marriage to the princess of Corinth. In her rage at this betrayal, Medea's love transformed into terrible vengeance. She murdered her own children and Jason's new bride with fire, then fled to Athens.

Medea exemplifies the destructive power of unchecked emotion and magic, and the consequences of abandonment in Greek tragedy. Jason was the hero she loved and helped but who devastated her through betrayal. The Argonauts, those legendary quest-seekers, succeeded only because of her magic and cunning. Theseus, the Athenian king, eventually gave her refuge after her vengeance in Corinth.
